title: Agent Architecture Cost-Success Trade-offs: A Controlled Evaluation across Enterprise-Style SOPs
abstract: arXiv:2611.12953v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Enterprises increasingly use large language model agents to execute standard operating procedures (SOPs): long, branching, tool-intensive workflows. Yet there is little controlled evidence for choosing among competing agentic architectures. Holding the model, tasks, and tools fixed and varying only the architecture, we compare four designs (a function-calling single agent, a skill-augmented agent, centralized multi-agent orchestration, and a triage swarm; eight arms) across 13 enterprise SOPs, and introduce a skill-definition quality rubric to build matched high and low-quality skill corpora. translated_title: 智能体架构的成本-成功率权衡：面向企业式标准操作流程的受控评估
translated_abstract: 企业越来越多地使用大型语言模型智能体来执行标准操作流程（SOP），即长链条、多分支、工具调用密集的工作流。然而，在相互竞争的智能体架构之间进行选择时，目前几乎没有受控的实证证据可供参考。我们在保持模型、任务和工具完全一致、仅改变架构的条件下，比较了四种设计（函数调用式单智能体、技能增强式智能体、集中式多智能体编排，以及分诊式智能体集群，共八种实验配置），覆盖13个企业SOP，并引入了一个技能定义质量评分标准，用于构建相互匹配的高质量与低质量技能语料库。研究得出三点结论：（1）不存在普遍最优的架构，正确的选择取决于具体的SOP。在同一SOP上，任务成功率从最难的不足10%到最容易的接近100%不等；从总体上看，没有任何架构在统计上显著可分，而更复杂的结构化设计似乎只有在复杂、多分支的SOP上才可能带来回报（直接……）
tldr: 该论文通过固定模型、任务与工具、仅改变架构的受控实验，在13个企业SOP上比较四种智能体架构，发现不存在普遍最优架构，架构选择应取决于具体SOP的复杂程度。
en_tdlr: This paper conducts controlled experiments—holding model, tasks, and tools fixed while varying only the architecture—to compare four agent designs across 13 enterprise SOPs, finding that there is no universally best architecture and that the right choice depends on the complexity of each specific SOP.
